name: Banach Fixed Point Theorem -- Canonical Sim
description: Constraint proof: contraction with k<1 admits unique fixed point

sympy_positive_convergence_rate.interpretation: contraction with k<1 exhibits exponential convergence

cvc5_positive_k_lt_1_admits_fixed_pt.test: cvc5 SAT: k < 1 AND exists fixed point
cvc5_positive_k_lt_1_admits_fixed_pt.interpretation: contraction property with k<1 is satisfiable with unique fixed point

numpy_positive_fixed_point_iteration.test: Fixed point iteration T(x)=0.5x+0.3 converges to x*=0.6
numpy_positive_fixed_point_iteration.interpretation: iteration trajectory converges exponentially to unique fixed point

cvc5_negative_k_geq_1_breaks_uniqueness.test: cvc5 attempt SAT: k ≥ 1 AND unique fixed point
cvc5_negative_k_geq_1_breaks_uniqueness.interpretation: k≥1 contradicts the uniqueness guarantee from contraction
cvc5_negative_k_geq_1_breaks_uniqueness.note: full UNSAT requires contraction property encoding

sympy_negative_k_geq_1_divergence.test: k ≥ 1 causes convergence formula to diverge/undefined
sympy_negative_k_geq_1_divergence.interpretation: Banach theorem constraint excludes k≥1 from providing unique fixed point

numpy_negative_k_geq_1_divergence.test: Iteration with k=1.1 diverges (not a contraction)
numpy_negative_k_geq_1_divergence.interpretation: non-contraction mapping does not converge to fixed point

sympy_boundary_k_approaching_1.test: Convergence rate as k approaches 1 from below

numpy_boundary_k_0p99_slow_convergence.interpretation: nearly-critical contraction (k close to 1) converges but slowly

sympy_boundary_limit_k_to_1_minus.test: Limit of convergence rate as k→1^-
sympy_boundary_limit_k_to_1_minus.interpretation: convergence rate diverges as k approaches 1 from below
